title: Checks for \0 escapes in string and byte literals that look like octal character escapes in C.
summary: C and other languages support octal character escapes in strings, where a backslash is followed by up to three octal digits. For example, \033 stands for the ASCII character 27 (ESC). Rust does not support this notation, but has the escape code \0 which stands for a null byte/character, and any following digits do not form part of the escape sequence. Therefore, \033 is not a compiler error but the result may be surprising. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.
